findings.claim: The plan checks only relative links, but OKF's recommended link form is bundle-relative (`/decisions/x.md`, resolved against the `.okf/` root; SPEC §6.1, and the okf skill says to prefer it). The plan does not say what happens to these links. If it skips them, the check misses the form OKF authors are told to use. If it resolves them against the repo or filesystem root, it reports working links as broken. The plan must say how `/` links resolve in `.okf/` (the bundle root) and in `docs/`.

The okf validator already checks `.okf/` cross-links (okf_validate.py check_links). It reports broken ones as warnings because OKF SPEC §6.1 says consumers MUST tolerate broken links, which may stand for knowledge not yet written. The parent ticket knowledge-check promises that `kmctl check` does not repeat what the okf validator checks. This plan makes a broken `.okf/` link a hard failure without addressing either point. The manifesto does list link checking as kmctl's job, so the scope can stay. But the plan should state its position: fail rather than warn, and why repeating the validator's `.okf/` check is acceptable, or limit the check to what the validator does not cover (for example `docs/`, and links that leave the bundle).
`/` links now have a defined meaning: in docs/ they resolve from the repository root, as GitHub renders them; in .okf/ they resolve from the bundle root (OKF §6.1) and are left to the validator.

The plan leaves in-bundle .okf/ links to the okf validator, which only warns as §6.1 requires, and fails only on docs/ links and .okf/ links that leave the bundle. A test checks that a broken in-bundle link is not reported.

In docs/README.md, _links drops every list-item line whole, so links the index check never looks at go unchecked: a list item linking ../CONTRIBUTING.md or /src/gone.py (which _entries discards as non-entries) and any second link on an entry line.
The kmctl check help text and the checks.py module summary line still say the command checks only indexes and prototypes; neither mentions the link check.

test_link_check_okf_links_leaving_bundle checks only the finding count and file, so an inverted check (good link reported, missing one not) still passes; it should also check the line or the message target.

Links that GitHub renders fine are reported as broken: percent-encoded paths (my%20page.md) and query strings (file.md?plain=1). Other links are skipped without notice: titles in single quotes, <angle brackets> with spaces, and reference-style [x][ref] definitions.

entries.change: On an index line only the entry link the index check reports is skipped, so other links on that line (outside the folder, root-relative, or a second link) are checked; the module docstring names the link check.
The kmctl check help now says it checks that links resolve.
A test for broken links on an index entry line, and the r3 test now asserts the exact line of the broken link.

findings.claim: docs/README.md list-item lines were skipped whole, hiding broken out-of-folder, / and second links
kmctl check help and the checks module docstring did not name the link check
the r3 test did not assert the exact finding line
